verdict: The hypothesis is partly right. Group A (closed partner models + Higgsfield prompts): Cinema Studio, Shorts Studio, Marketing Studio Image, Ads Studio, Upscale, Fashion Factory steps 4-5, Genjutsu (likely Seedance 2.5), Genjutsu Lite (likely Wan 3.0), Effects 2.0 chains, Evolution, Mirelo / Sonilo. Group B (open models + public LoRAs under a Higgsfield name, confirmed): Angles, Animate / Recast, Infinite Talk, Depth Map, Remove Background. Group C (self-hosted diffusion models with LoRA presets and per-user fine-tunes): Soul v1, Soul 2.0, Soul Cinema, Soul ID, moodboards, DoP, Speak v1, Popcorn / Instadump. In group C the LoRA mechanism is confirmed in code, but the base checkpoints are not public; fingerprints point to the Wan family for DoP, Soul v1's current backend and Popcorn.

crossCutting.claim: Higgsfield describes itself as building 'its own tools, Cinema Studio among them and its own models, such as Soul, on top of interchangeable, best-in-class generation models'.

Higgsfield describes Soul 2.0 as 'Higgsfield's own foundation image model, built in-house' tuned by 'training on the actual subject matter'. This conflicts in tone with the statement above; neither names a base model.

The help center lists 'Higgsfield DoP ... alongside Soul, Popcorn, and Cinema Studio' as Higgsfield's own proprietary models, while the Cinema Studio article says 'Cinema Studio 4.0 runs on Seedance 2.5'. So 'proprietary' on Higgsfield includes products that run on a partner model.
The Series B post says Higgsfield 'add[s] a production layer around models through workflow tooling, cinematic controls, proprietary technology and automated production systems'.

Prompt Engineer job: 'Develop product use cases and one-click presets for generative image/video models', 'complex generative content pipelines', 'General knowledge of ComfyUI pipelines'. Presets are built by prompt engineers.

Data Scientist job: 'Want to train or fine-tune generative video models — that's what our R&D ML Engineer roles do'. ML Security job: 'GPU clusters supporting distributed training and production inference across cloud and rented datacenter environments'. Higgsfield trains or fine-tunes some video models and serves models on its own GPUs.
None of the 96 roles on the public job board on 2026-10-23 is a research-scientist role for pre-training image or video foundation models (ML roles are Ads, Security, AI Engineer, Prompt Engineer).

The company's older open-source work is a distributed fine-tuning framework ('higgsfield', GPU orchestration for training LLMs, GitHub org higgsfield-ai) and a 2023 Hugging Face org with dozens of Mistral-7B and Llama-2 fine-tunes. Fine-tuning open weights is the company's original skill.

The web client calls many products by a Higgsfield name while the job type names the open model underneath: QWEN_CAMERA_CONTROL = 'Higgsfield Angles'; WAN2_2_ANIMATE / WAN2_2_ANIMATE_V2 = 'Higgsfield Animate' in one label function (XQvVauJI5fIVvC8i.js) but 'Wan 2.2 Animate' / 'Wan 2.2 Animate V2' in the main label map (j-8rpwEzEMqpgGav.js, which also has WAN2_2_ANIMATE_FACESWAP = 'Wan 2.2 Faceswap'); WAN2_2_ANIMATE_V3 / WAN2_2_ANIMATE_REVOICE = 'Higgsfield Recast'; NANO_BANANA_OUTFIT_COLLAGE = 'Higgsfield Outfit Collage'; IMAGE2VIDEO_EXTEND = 'Higgsfield Speak'; IMAGE2VIDEO_MIX = 'Higgsfield Mix Motion'; TEXT2KEYFRAMES = 'Higgsfield Popcorn'.

Terms of Use, last updated 2026-10-23: section 5.1(iii) bars using the Service or any Outputs 'to develop, modify, fine-tune, distill, or improve any products or services that compete with the Service, including any artificial intelligence or machine-learning algorithms or models of any kind'; section 5.2(iv) bars using 'the Service, any Outputs, or any data derived therefrom to train, fine-tune, distill, or otherwise transfer knowledge to any machine-learning model, neural network, or artificial intelligence system, whether or not such system competes with the Service' (exceptions: models trained on your own Inputs, or written permission); section 5.2(v) bars any attempt to 'decompile, distill, reverse compile, or reverse engineer any part of the Service'. Fuobe must not train LoRAs on Higgsfield preset previews or generations, and uses client-code findings only as facts, never as copied code, prompts or media.

evidence.claim: Higgsfield calls Soul its 'native model for cinematic and fashion looks' and launched it on 2025-06-25 as a 'high-aesthetic photo model' with 50+ presets.

Soul v1 is a diffusion sampler Higgsfield runs itself: the form 'hf:soul-form-09-13' carries steps 50, sampleShift 3, sampleGuideScale 4, an empty negativePrompt, version 3, apg_eta 0 (Adaptive Projected Guidance), compile true (torch.compile) and a staff flag use_green; the staff-only key list is soul: [sampleGuideScale, sampleShift, use_apg, compile, apg_eta, use_green].

Those defaults are identical to Higgsfield's own 'Wan 2.2' image form (hf:wan2.2-image-form: steps 50, sampleShift 3, sampleGuideScale 4, negativePrompt '', version 3, apg_eta 0), and both forms size images with the same shared function. The Wan 2.2 image grid is 1536x1536 at the '720p' tier, which is the size the legacy Soul API example uses ('1536x1536'). The current Soul v1 backend (version 3) shares the Wan 2.2 image pipeline.

Soul v1's weights are a Wan 2.2 fine-tune. Only fingerprints point that way (shared defaults, Wan CLI names sample_shift / sample_guide_scale). Soul v1 launched 2025-06-25, before Wan 2.2 (released 2025-07-28), so the launch model was something else and the backend has been swapped since ('version 3').

Presets behave like stacked adapters: each request has style_id + style_strength 0-1 and custom_reference_id + custom_reference_strength 0-1; strength 0 'uses the selected style's default character strength'; behind a client flag, picking a character sends preset strength 0.6 and character strength 0.9.

evidence.claim: Higgsfield calls Soul 2.0 'Higgsfield's own foundation image model, built in-house for fashion-aware, culture-native image generation', and admits a weakness: 'the trained face can end up cloned onto background people in a scene'.

Every Soul 2.0 and Soul Cinema style record carries 'lora' and 'lora_2' fields. A staff-only panel lists them as 'LoRA 1: <name>' and 'LoRA 2: <name>' next to '(Dev) Preset Strength' and '(Dev) Character Strength' sliders (0-1).
So each Soul 2.0 preset is one or two LoRAs applied to a shared base model, with preset strength and character strength as LoRA scales.

The Soul 2.0 request (form hf:soul-v2-form-01-dev-upd) sends model soul_v2, width/height (longest side capped at 2048, rounded to 16), aspect_ratio, prompt, negative_prompt, enhance_prompt, style_id, style_strength, custom_reference_id + strength, colour signature, use_refiner (off), use_green (on), use_green_aidar (off), lora, chain_enhancer, time_denoise_from (0.83 per image in one path) and model_version 'fast'.

Reading of those fields: a negative prompt means a CFG model; 'time_denoise_from 0.83' and 'use_refiner' mean a second pass that re-noises the first result; 'model_version fast' means a distilled variant; 'use_green_aidar' names a staff member, so these are in-house experiment switches.

Soul 2.0 requests can also carry use_olzhas, use_sultan or use_aidar (one per request, chosen by a staff selector), and time_denoise_from is filled with 0.83 for every image in the batch. These are model variants named after staff members.

Moodboards are trained the same way presets are stored: POST /custom-references/soul-v2-preset {name, input_images} with states In queue, In progress, Preparing cover, Complete. Curated moodboards are the same kind of trained style artifact (a style LoRA).

Price: 0.125 credits (about $0.006) per image on the web; API $0.0032 (720p) / $0.0057 (1080p). That is cheaper than Higgsfield's own resale of Z-Image Turbo ($0.015). The base is a small or distilled model that Higgsfield serves itself.

The trained artifact is a LoRA-style adapter per person and per model family: separate endpoints per family, /custom-references/retrain {custom_reference_id, input_images, target_type} and 'Upgrade Character', a 3-5 minute train, and the admitted background face cloning (identity bleed) all fit a LoRA.

Launched 2025-03-31 as 'DoP I2V-01-preview' with thanks to Nebius and TensorWave (AMD MI300X); Higgsfield's launch blog (now 404) said it 'blends diffusion models with reinforcement learning' with RL applied after diffusion. Wan 2.1 open weights had been released five weeks earlier (2025-02-25).

evidence.claim: DoP form 'hf:create:video:hf': frames 49 ('3s') or 81 ('5s'), steps 30, motionIds + motionStrengths, strength 1, guideScale, sampleShift. Preset pages carry settings {steps:20, frames:81, strength:1, guide_scale:6} and presetFamily 'higgsfield'.

49 frames = 3 s and 81 frames = 5 s means 16 fps, the native output of Wan 2.1 / 2.2 14B (Wan configs: frame_num 81, sample_fps 16), and the knobs use Wan's names (sample shift, guide scale). DoP is a Wan-14B-lineage image-to-video model.

The motion picker treats any motion id ending in '.safetensors' as a raw LoRA file ('loras/<name>.safetensors', shown under the model label 'Higgsfield Canary'), and a staff 'canary' channel lists such motions for image2video and avatar. Such an id is sent as `reference` (type 'reference') instead of `motion_id`. DoP motions and LoRA files are interchangeable in the client.
